question: Suppose a model had no attention layers at all. What would happen to the meaning of "king" in "She looked across the board and said, triumphantly, 'King me'"?

options.text: It would stay where the embedding put it, among monarchs, whatever the surrounding words said
options.feedback: The embedding is a first guess made in isolation, and attention is the only mechanism that lets the other words move it. Without attention, "board" and "triumphantly" would have no way to reach "king".

options.text: The MLP (multi-layer perceptron) would use the surrounding words to move it toward checkers instead
options.feedback: The MLP works only on the embedding it is handed and applies what it learned in training; it does not read the other words in the context. Gathering from the context is attention's job, and nothing else does it.

options.text: The token encoding would switch to the verb form of "king" to compensate
options.feedback: Token encoding assigns the same number to "king" regardless of sense, and it happens before any meaning is worked out. It cannot respond to context.

options.text: The model would be unable to produce a next token for the sentence
options.feedback: The pipeline would still run and still produce probabilities; it would just do so with a poor sense of what each word means here. The failure would be a worse guess, not no guess.
